_doc: MARKET-1 (owner, 2026-11-12): components, competitor coverage, users, stories and objections as data. Every feature claim has a proof probe and a test; every gap has a closing probe and becomes a queue item (docs/issues/Q-GAP-*.json) the executor works; the build fails if a claimed feature loses its proof or a gap quietly closes. INTERNAL: confidentiality rules apply, nothing here is published on the site. Competitor facts come only from the sources listed, read 2026-11-12; 'none-found' means the source was silent, not that the capability is absent. Read by foundation/market.py.

components.name: Idea intake
components.what: Turning a few spoken or typed words from someone who does not code into a scoped job, with the forks surfaced as questions.

alternatives.name: Lovable, Bolt.new, v0, Replit, Base44
alternatives.note: All take a prompt and produce an app; the comparison lists build, hosting, database and deploy for each.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare VibeSDK
alternatives.note: Describe an app in plain language; it generates, previews and deploys it on Cloudflare.

components.integration_gap: Prompt boxes end at the first build. None of the sources read describes intake that carries on as the standing direction for later work.

components.name: Planning and anticipating forks
components.what: Breaking an idea into work items and the branching paths (accounts, data, money, domains) before they bite.

alternatives.name: Factory Droids
alternatives.note: Specs from Slack threads, codebase research and Linear prioritisation for engineering teams.

components.integration_gap: Planning agents work on an existing engineering org's tickets; the sources read show none that plans from a non-coder's first sentence.

components.name: Code and repository
components.what: Writing the change, a branch and a pull request.

alternatives.name: GitHub Copilot coding agent
alternatives.note: Researches, plans, edits, runs tests and opens one pull request per task, in the background.

alternatives.name: Claude Code scheduled tasks
alternatives.note: Cloud sessions run a prompt against repositories and push claude/ branches.

alternatives.name: Factory Droids
alternatives.note: Builds features end to end from a ticket, spec or prompt.

components.integration_gap: Coding agents are strong here and Ultrastable does not claim to beat them; it hands work to them. Its own executor opening a merged PR is still pinned.

components.name: Backend, hosting and infrastructure
components.what: Where it runs, the database, the domain, deploys.

alternatives.name: Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, Base44
alternatives.note: Hosting, database and deployment inside the product.

alternatives.name: v0
alternatives.note: Deploys via Vercel; the comparison says backend and data often need external services.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare VibeSDK
alternatives.note: Per-app Workers, sandboxes, one-click export to GitHub or a Cloudflare account.

components.integration_gap: Sites Ultrastable builds today have no shared back end and live at a shared address. Both are open gaps.

components.name: Front end people already know
components.what: A familiar interface for non-coders that stays out of an engineer's way.

alternatives.name: App builders
alternatives.note: Chat-style prompt interfaces are the norm.

components.integration_gap: Familiar chat is table stakes. The differentiator is the same thread reaching the repo, the infrastructure and the running loops.

components.name: Many agents, one ledger
components.what: Several coding agents and roles taking work without editing the same thing.

alternatives.name: GitHub Copilot with Claude and Codex agents
alternatives.note: GitHub's changelog reports Claude and Codex available alongside Copilot.

components.integration_gap: Not found in the sources read: a neutral claim ledger across agents from different vendors.

components.name: Self-closing loops
components.what: Work that continues on a heartbeat: pick, do, verify, write back, with no person in the path.

alternatives.name: Claude Code scheduled tasks
alternatives.note: Schedule, API and GitHub triggers run cloud sessions unattended; research preview, tied to an individual account, with hourly caps.

alternatives.name: Copilot automations and Agent Merge
alternatives.note: Scheduled or event-driven tasks and automatic fixing of failed Actions or merge conflicts on a watched PR.

alternatives.name: Zapier Agents and n8n
alternatives.note: Automations with agents; a practitioner source reports failures and lost context in multi-step chains.

components.integration_gap: Each product runs loops over its own surface. Defensible claim: none of the sources read closes the loop across idea, repo, infrastructure and operations under one verified registry.

components.name: Verification and rollback
components.what: Proving a change worked and undoing it without a person.

alternatives.name: Copilot coding agent
alternatives.note: Docs state its output can be incorrect or insecure and must be reviewed and tested by the user.

components.integration_gap: Not found in the sources read: automatic revert on a failed post-deploy probe, or a second model grading the build against the brief.

components.name: Trust and permissions
components.what: What each agent may do, widened by track record and bounded by a closed boundary.

alternatives.name: Claude Code auto mode
alternatives.note: A classifier allows or blocks actions during unattended runs; branch and connector scope limit blast radius.

components.integration_gap: Per-agent permission is common. Earned, scored trust per surface and action, with a machine-read inside/egress boundary, was not found in the sources read.

components.name: Keeping it running
components.what: Monitoring, incidents, metrics and scoring whether decisions were right.

alternatives.name: Factory Droids
alternatives.note: On-call incident resolution, alert triage and root cause analysis.

alternatives.name: App builders
alternatives.note: The comparison source does not cover monitoring or maintenance after launch; that is silence in one source, not proof they lack it.

components.integration_gap: Prediction scoring is run by the system on itself; an outside audit is pinned and must not be claimed.

components.name: Any infrastructure
components.what: Running on more than one cloud or host.

alternatives.name: Cloudflare VibeSDK
alternatives.note: Cloudflare only, with code export.

alternatives.name: Copilot coding agent
alternatives.note: GitHub-hosted repositories only.

components.integration_gap: Only Cloudflare is proven in production for Ultrastable. Briefs for other clouds exist but are untested.

features.name: Chat-thread front door with pill input and dictation
features.note: Dictation has not been exercised with real audio.

features.name: Rotating suggestions that respond to what is typed
Idea to live page with no account or terminal
Second-model audit with an honest list of what could not be done
Change requests in the same thread
Click-only guided setup of a personal project
Engineer lane with honest Live/Testing/Pinned status
Ten-minute heartbeat that claims and dispatches work
Claim ledger across agents with stale-claim release
Closed-loop axiom enforced in every instruction file
Post-deploy probes with automatic revert
features.note: Test file is the site gate; the probe runner has its own checks in the platform tree.

features.name: Trust ledger per surface and action
Machine-read containment boundary with rebuild drill
Predictions logged before action and scored later
Deploy briefs for other clouds
features.note: Only Cloudflare is proven in production.

features.name: Executor opens its own merged pull request
features.note: Pull requests 749 and 762 were opened by the executor and merged on 2026-11-20; both were mechanical fixes, none written by a model yet.

features.name: Next question chosen from the answers so far
features.note: The next question is chosen from the answers so far: a bound model proposes it, a deterministic rule table is the floor, at most four questions (ADAPTIVE-1).

gaps.title: Wrap loops around an existing repository
gaps.why: Engineers and vibe-coders arrive with a repo, not an idea.

gaps.title: Shared back end for built sites
gaps.why: Built sites keep data only in the visitor's browser.

gaps.title: Attach the person's own domain
gaps.why: Built sites live at a shared Ultrastable address.

gaps.title: Set up a full organization from the thread
gaps.why: The thread builds a site; the organization around it is still set up through /setup.

gaps.title: Executor opens and merges its own pull request
gaps.why: The executor opens pull requests with real models (five by 2026-11-20); none has merged yet. The log on main records each outcome (PR-OUTCOME-1).

gaps.title: Re-score predictions with a second model
gaps.why: Prediction scoring is self-run; a held-out grader narrows that before any outside audit.

gaps.title: Prove one non-Cloudflare cloud end to end
gaps.why: Briefs exist; nothing is proven off Cloudflare.

gaps.title: An agent run that survives a restart and resumes from its last completed step
gaps.why: A claimed item whose agent dies part-way is released by reap_claims and started again from the beginning; nothing resumes from the last completed step.
gaps.evidence: Cloudflare Agents (recoverable execution), LangGraph (durable execution, checkpointers), Temporal (Durable Execution) and CrewAI (checkpointing) each state it on their own pages, read 2026-11-26.

gaps.title: Hand a task to the system from a team chat
gaps.why: Work enters through the front door, the repository form, the work API and the owner console; a team chat is not an entry point.
gaps.evidence: Devin, GitHub Copilot cloud agent, Cursor, Codex, Lovable and v0 each list a Slack or Teams integration on their own pages, read 2026-11-26.

gaps.title: The platform site answers MCP and A2A the way the kit now does
gaps.why: The kit answers an unsupported MCP version with UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) and serves an A2A 1.0 card without legacy fields; site/agentic.js still answers -32600 and its card carries the 0.3 fields url, preferredTransport and additionalInterfaces.
gaps.evidence: MCP 2026-07-28 versioning page and A2A 1.0 specification section 4.4.1, read 2026-11-26.

gaps.title: Competitor capabilities are evidenced by a sentence of the page body, not by a navigation word
gaps.why: The R&D taxonomy matches one regular expression per capability over the whole page text, so a menu entry such as "Azure DevOps" or "Pull requests" counts as evidence of other-cloud or autonomous-pr; 2026-11-26 profiles show both.

users.persona: Person with an idea who has never coded
users.needs: Say it, see it live, change it by talking.

stories.story: As someone who has never coded, I say a few words and get a live page, so I can show people my idea today.
As that person, I see what was checked and what could not be done, so I know what to trust.
As that person, I tell the thread what to change and watch it happen.
As that person, I want the site to use my own address and remember what visitors enter.
As someone who is not sure what I want, the questions adapt to what I already said instead of following a fixed list.

users.persona: Small-business owner who needs it kept running
users.needs: It must keep working without hiring anyone.

stories.story: As an owner, a broken deploy undoes itself and I do not have to notice.
As an owner, I want the whole organization set up by talking, not by a wizard.

users.persona: Vibe coder whose app works but nobody maintains it
users.needs: Something to keep what they built alive and improving.

stories.story: As a vibe coder, I point Ultrastable at what I built and it starts looking after it.
As a vibe coder, the system chooses and verifies its own next task.

users.persona: Engineer or team lead who already uses coding agents
users.needs: Loops, claims and proof around the agents they have.

stories.story: As an engineer, several agents take work through one claim ledger, so two never edit the same file.
As an engineer, trust is earned per surface and action and a closed boundary limits blast radius.
As an engineer, I can skip the interview and read honest Live, Testing and Pinned status.
As an engineer, an agent run that dies part-way resumes from its last completed step, so a long task is not started over.
As an engineer, I hand a task to the system from the team chat I already use.
As an engineer, my MCP or A2A client gets the same answers from the platform site as from any system built with the kit.

users.persona: Funder or grant reviewer judging whether this is real
users.needs: Claims that are measured, with limits stated.

stories.story: As a reviewer, every claim has a live check and every limit is stated.
As a reviewer, I see the system run on more than one cloud.

objections.objection: Isn't this just a code agent?
objections.answer: No. Coding agents write the change. Ultrastable decides what to work on, hands each task to the agent that fits, proves the result live, reverts it on a failed probe, and records whether its own prediction was right. It sits around coding agents rather than competing with them.
objections.concede: The coding agents named in this file are strong at writing the change, and the only pull requests Ultrastable's own executor has opened and merged so far are mechanical fixes, not changes written by a model.

objections.objection: Surely Claude Code has thought of this.
objections.answer: Claude Code now runs unattended scheduled tasks on schedule, API and GitHub triggers, so loops exist there. The sources read show those loops tied to one individual's account, in research preview, working on repositories. What was not found is one verified registry that closes the loop across intake, repository, infrastructure and operations, with earned trust and a scored track record.
objections.concede: Scheduled cloud tasks are real and overlap the heartbeat. Say 'in the sources we read', never 'nobody does'.

objections.objection: GitHub Copilot already assigns issues to agents.
objections.answer: True, and it can fix failed Actions runs on a watched PR. It works on GitHub repositories, one branch and one PR per task, and its documentation says output must be reviewed and tested. Ultrastable adds the idea-to-running-system path and automatic probes and revert.
objections.concede: On GitHub-hosted code Copilot's agent is a direct alternative for the code step.

objections.objection: Lovable, Bolt and Replit already turn ideas into apps.
objections.answer: They do, with hosting and databases. The comparison read for this file does not cover what happens after launch. Ultrastable's pitch is the after: it keeps the thing running and improving, and says what it could not do.
objections.concede: Prompt-to-app is table stakes and they are polished at it. Absence of monitoring in one comparison is not proof they lack it.

objections.objection: Cloudflare open-sourced a vibe coding platform.
objections.answer: VibeSDK generates, previews and deploys apps on Cloudflare and exports code. Ultrastable runs on Cloudflare as well and is complementary, since VibeSDK describes no post-deploy operation.
objections.concede: VibeSDK covers intake to deploy on the same infrastructure; the announcement does not state what happens after deploy.

objections.objection: Zapier Agents and n8n automate things already.
objections.answer: They connect services and run flows. They are not described in the source read as writing or maintaining code or hosting what a person asked for.
objections.concede: The only source read for them is a secondary, anecdotal practitioner write-up.

objections.answer: The live checks on the proof page are measured. One installation exists; prediction scoring is self-run; other clouds are untested. Those limits are in the engineer lane and in the gaps listed here.
objections.concede: No second installation, no outside audit, no off-Cloudflare proof yet.

rationale: Q-GROW-second-tenant-deploying: prove the product beyond tenant 0 with a second tenant running its own unattended deploy loop (target: tenant_systems_deploying_unattended = 3 on systems-running).
